title: Signal Drift
premise: A glowing relay core drifts through a hazardous space field, recovering scattered signal shards while avoiding destructive debris.
interaction_model: Single-screen canvas arcade game with horizontal pointer/touch steering; tap or drag to move the player core left and right.
objective: Collect as many signal shards as possible for score while avoiding debris that ends the run on contact.
progression: The run starts immediately, obstacle speed and spawn pressure gradually increase with distance, story-text callouts update over time, and the player restarts after a single-hit game over.
theme: Minimalist sci-fi signal-recovery mission in deep space.
mood: Tense, sleek, atmospheric, and arcade-driven with soft holographic UI feedback.
likely_audience: Players who enjoy fast mobile-friendly reflex games, score chasers, and lightweight sci-fi arcade experiences.
confidence_notes: High confidence that the core loop is collect-beneficial-items while dodging hazards in an endless survival format.
High confidence that the intended platform is mobile web because of pointer controls, safe-area padding, vibration hooks, and touch-friendly layout.
Moderate confidence in labeling it as a runner variant, since forward movement is implied through scrolling objects and distance rather than explicit travel controls.
recreation_prompt: Recreate a polished mobile-first HTML5 arcade game called "Signal Drift" where the player controls a glowing sci-fi relay core near the bottom of the screen and steers it left and right by tapping or dragging horizontally. The goal is to survive as long as possible in a dark deep-space field while collecting falling signal shards for points and avoiding falling debris that destroys the relay in one hit. Present the game as a single-screen endless survival run with a canvas-based playfield, subtle lane guides, drifting stars, a moody blue-black gradient background, and holographic HUD panels showing a score readout, short mission/story text, and contextual feedback messages. Make collectibles visually bright, geometric, and inviting, while hazards feel jagged, metallic, and dangerous. Increase difficulty over time by raising fall speed and spawn density as the run continues. Add satisfying collection feedback with particles, sound, optional vibration, and a brief celebratory overlay, and use stronger fail feedback plus a game-over overlay with final score and a restart button when the player collides with debris. Keep the tone atmospheric, sleek, and readable, with short run-based score chasing, instant restarts, and controls that feel smooth and forgiving on mobile.
